x: We are half way through our track season here and I'm doing quite well, although the winter season with its longer distances always suit me better. Hope we see Carl over this way next year for the Commonwealth Games, or perhaps even Ray. If ever a fellow deserves a trip it's Ray.
Our third and fourth scorers did well to bring us second place - not bad for Ray and John Bromley who, between them have carried the Bels colours for over fifty years!
Carl was in the leading group with John well placed and it wasn't long before Allan came through with Ray moving strongly to complete our four.

Carl walked well for 6th place and then came a flush of Steyning and Sheffield vests. Allan was our next man then Ray - but where was John Hall? Alas he had been disqualified and obviously it was no medals this time.

Making his debut over the distance was Trevor McDermot who walked the first half with Ray and then showed us what a prospect he is by dropping Ray (his second 10kms was faster than his first), to get under 110 minutes.
Charlie Manning opts out because programme does not carry Government Health Warning. Take this game seriously?- I don't even take Ray seriously. John Bicourt-not running-go back three places.

His first reaction was to ask his son Ray, to help him continue the collections. According to Lily, this injury prompted the stroke from which he was to die three years later on, one day short of his 81st birthday.

Also offering assistance as dawn broke were fellow Belgravians Carl Lawton, George Beecham and Ray Middleton. Paul stuck to the task and gradually got back into his stride managing to achieve the target with some time to spare and thus join that select band of Belgravians who have qualified to call…

Dave McMillan first won the title in 1974 and then had to wait another 30 years before he claimed it again, beating Cynthia James. This year the James Gang had another finalist in Ray – but Dave again carried off the pot for his third win all told.
